name: Estonia
summary: Three MNOs – Telia Eesti, Elisa Eesti and Tele2 Eesti – with 5G spectrum from TTJA auctions of 3.5 GHz (2022), 700 MHz (2022) and 26 GHz (2023). Estonian licences are renewed yearly as long as fees are paid.

operators.name: Tele2
operators.notes: Subsidiary of Tele2 AB. Bought Televõrgu AS and ST-Network OÜ (2.3 GHz) in 2016–17 and a second 2.1 GHz licence from Raadiovõrk OÜ in 2014.

operators.name: Bitė
operators.notes: Lithuanian operator; not an Estonian MNO. Qualified for the 2022 Estonian 3.5 GHz auction but won nothing. The seed lists a non-commercial 2.3 GHz licence.

bands.label: 450 MHz
bands.note: Nationwide CDMA-450 service ended in 2016. In 2023 MKM/TTJA consulted on a competition for one 2×5 MHz licence in 410 or 450 MHz for critical-infrastructure/utility networks; no award was found. Tele2's Dec-2025 portfolio no longer lists an Estonian 450 MHz licence.

bands.label: 700 MHz FDD (B28/n28)
bands.note: TTJA auctioned six 2×5 MHz blocks in Nov 2022; each operator won two (2×10 MHz). Amounts confirmed by TTJA via ERR; block order from the davwheat seed, consistent with the listed NR-ARFCNs.

blocks.notes: Two 2×5 MHz licences, Nov 2022 auction, €2.011m; LTE + NR (DSS)

bands.label: 800 MHz (B20)
bands.note: Edges from the davwheat seed, which cited TTJA licence pages in the old JVIS/MTR registers (no longer publicly reachable); Tele2's 2×10 MHz is confirmed by its investor spectrum table.

bands.label: 850 MHz (B5)
bands.note: Not a European mobile band.

bands.label: 600 MHz (B71)
bands.note: Not assigned: 470–694 MHz is used for DTT broadcasting; the US 600 MHz plan is not used in Europe.

bands.label: 900 MHz (B8)
bands.note: Edges from the davwheat seed, which cited TTJA licence pages in the old JVIS/MTR registers (no longer publicly reachable); Tele2 reports 2×11.4 MHz (seed edges give 2×11.6 MHz; the 0.2 MHz difference is probably an unassigned guard).

bands.label: 1.4 GHz L-band SDL (B32/B75)
bands.note: No 1.4 GHz licence found: TTJA's auction pages list no L-band competition and no operator reports holdings.

bands.label: AWS 1.7/2.1 GHz (B4/B66)
bands.note: Not a European band plan.

bands.label: 1800 MHz (B3)
bands.note: Edges from the davwheat seed, which cited TTJA licence pages in the old JVIS/MTR registers (no longer publicly reachable); Tele2 reports 2×24.8 MHz vs 2×25.0 MHz in the seed edges.

bands.label: PCS 1900 (B2/B25)
bands.note: Not a European band plan.

bands.label: 1.9 GHz TDD (B39)
bands.note: Edges from the davwheat seed, which cited TTJA licence pages in the old JVIS/MTR registers (no longer publicly reachable); Tele2 reports '2×29.8 + 10 TDD' in the 2.1 GHz band, confirming its 10 MHz unpaired block.

bands.label: 2100 MHz (B1/n1)
bands.note: Edges from the davwheat seed, which cited TTJA licence pages in the old JVIS/MTR registers (no longer publicly reachable); Tele2 reports 2×29.8 MHz vs 2×30 MHz in the seed edges.

blocks.notes: Includes second licence bought from Raadiovõrk OÜ in 2014

bands.label: 2300 MHz (B40/n40)
bands.note: Tele2's 60 MHz is confirmed by Tele2 (investor table) and by TTJA via ERR (2022). A 2.3 GHz tender was consulted on in 2023; no result was found.

blocks.notes: Two 30 MHz licences acquired with Televõrgu AS and ST-Network OÜ (2016–17); the ST-Network block was moved from 2360–2390 to 2330–2360 MHz in 2017
Seed lists a non-commercial licence to Bitė here; TTJA told ERR in 2022 that 2360–2390 MHz is also used for national defence. Not verified

bands.label: 2600 MHz FDD (B7/n7)
bands.note: Edges from the davwheat seed, which cited TTJA licence pages in the old JVIS/MTR registers (no longer publicly reachable); Tele2 holds no 2.6 GHz spectrum in Estonia (per its investor table).

bands.label: 2600 MHz TDD (B38/n38)
bands.note: Edges from the davwheat seed, which cited TTJA licence pages in the old JVIS/MTR registers (no longer publicly reachable); the 2575–2615 MHz lot is named in the 2019 competition regulation.

bands.label: 3.4–3.8 GHz (n78)
bands.note: Each licence is 130 MHz in two parts ('before transition'). After the transition set in the auction rules the licences become contiguous: I 3410–3540, II 3540–3670, III 3670–3800 MHz. No evidence was found that the transition has happened.

blocks.notes: Licence I, part 2; use restricted near the Russian border
Licence II, part 2; use restricted near the Russian border
Licence III, part 2; use restricted near the Russian border

bands.label: 4.4–5.0 GHz (n79)
bands.note: Not assigned; not harmonised for mobile in Europe.

bands.label: 26 GHz (n258)
bands.note: Six 400 MHz lots in 24.7–27.1 GHz were auctioned on 10 May 2023; each operator won two. Tele2 states its block is 24.7–25.5 GHz; the Elisa/Telia positions were not found.

holdings.notes: Two 400 MHz licences, €1.600m; Tele2 says it operates at 24.7–25.5 GHz

bands.label: 40 GHz (n259/n260)
bands.note: Not assigned: TTJA's competition pages list no 40 GHz award.

bands.label: 47 GHz (n262)
bands.note: Not assigned: TTJA's competition pages list no 47 GHz award.

notes: The TTJA licence registers the seed cited (jvis.ttja.ee/modules/sideluba/avalik/view/…, mtr.ttja.ee) are no longer publicly accessible (404, or the MTR app is closed). Block edges below 3.5 GHz therefore remain 'unverified' seed values, cross-checked only for amounts against Tele2's investor spectrum table (updated 29 Dec 2025).

Small conflicts: Tele2 reports 2×11.4 (900), 2×24.8 (1800) and 2×29.8 MHz (2100), while the seed edges give 2×11.6, 2×25.0 and 2×30.0 MHz. The seed edges are kept; the differences are probably guard slivers.

3.5 GHz licences (2022): Elisa €7.2m (licence I), Telia €8.5m (licence II), Tele2 about €1.6m (licence III); starting price €1.597m. Each licence consists of two parts until a transition to contiguous 130 MHz blocks (the transition relates to restrictions near the Russian border).
Tele2's investor table notes that Estonian licences are renewed yearly if fees are paid, so no expiry dates are given.
missing: Regulator-confirmed block edges for 800, 900, 1800, 2100, 2.6 GHz FDD/TDD, B39 TDD and 2.3 GHz (the TTJA public licence register was unreachable).
Whether the 3.5 GHz transition to contiguous 3410–3540/3540–3670/3670–3800 MHz blocks has taken effect.
26 GHz block positions for Elisa and Telia (Tele2: 24.7–25.5 GHz per operator).

changes: Renamed operators to brands (Telia, Elisa, Tele2) with legal names; merged the duplicate 'UAB Bite Lietuva'/'Bite' entries into one 'Bitė' (kind other).
Downgraded all seed bands except 3.5 GHz from verified to unverified: the cited TTJA register pages now return 404.
3.5 GHz: confirmed licence I/II/III ranges and winners from TTJA's competition page and ERR; documented the pending transition to contiguous blocks.
700 MHz: added the Nov 2022 auction result (each operator 2×10 MHz, prices).
2300 MHz: added the history of Tele2's two 30 MHz blocks and the defence use of 2360–2390 MHz; drew 2390–2400 MHz as unassigned.
Added 26 GHz (2023 auction; 800 MHz each, holdings), 450 MHz (unknown), and not-assigned entries for 600/850/1400/1700/1900/4900/40/47 GHz.
2.6 GHz TDD: drew the 2570–2575 and 2615–2620 MHz guards explicitly.
